clue.text: Work occupies troublesome Luther in cell

indicators.note: the work settles inside the jumbled letters, as a tenant occupies a house
troublesome suggests the letters of Luther and in are unruly and rearranged

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A rebellious Martin Luther is kept busy writing while locked in a monastic cell.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled letters come out as NEUTRHIL before the work goes in. 'cell' is not a prison or monk's room but a biological one.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutrophil is a type of white blood cell that fights infection.

clue.text: Nine months packed with tension and hesitation

parts.note: packed means crammed, full
T is a standard abbreviation for tension in physics
erm is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A pregnancy's long wait is filled with stress and uncertainty.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun phrase standing for the period a full-term pregnancy completes.
explanation.definitionFit: A full-term pregnancy has lasted the whole normal span of about nine months.

clue.text: Describe being free of fearsome old Scottish people?

parts.note: the prefix de- means removing or freeing from, as in de-ice
the Picts were a warlike ancient people of northern Scotland; one of them is a Pict

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about ridding the land of ancient Scottish warriors.
explanation.walkthrough: A playful split: DE-PICT read as 'rid of Picts', the painted tribes of early Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict something is to portray or represent it in words or pictures.

clue.text: Regularly praises exam success

indicators.note: regularly picks letters at even intervals, here every other one starting with the first of praises

explanation.surface: A student is often praised for doing well in examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of 'praises'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass is the grade awarded when a candidate succeeds in a test.

clue.text: Conservative succession secured by Nazi police plots

indicators.note: secured by means held fast within, so the other pieces sit between the police letters

parts.note: the SS was the Nazi paramilitary police force
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
a line is a succession, as in a line of kings

explanation.surface: A wartime political thriller: the Tory line of succession held hostage by the Gestapo.
explanation.definitionFit: Storylines are the plots of novels, films or dramas, the sequence of events narrated.

clue.text: Go up to the bar twice for Skol

indicators.note: twice means the piece appears two times in a row

parts.note: to chin a bar is to pull yourself up until your chin is over it, as in a chin-up

explanation.surface: Heading to the pub counter repeatedly to raise a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub but is a gym bar. Skol is a Scandinavian drinking toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal toasts said when raising glasses, a Scandinavian one and a British one.

clue.text: Lancaster House?

parts.note: Lancaster House is a London mansion, but read as the shelter that houses an Avro Lancaster bomber it means an aircraft shed

explanation.surface: Simply the name of a grand London government mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lancaster was a famous Second World War bomber; the question mark signals the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangar is the large building where aircraft are housed and maintained.

clue.text: Vain creep needing no introduction

indicators.note: no introduction means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to sidle is to creep along furtively

explanation.surface: A conceited sneak who thinks everyone already knows who he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' drops the S from SIDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain in the sense of futile or pointless matches idle, as in idle threats.

clue.text: Lively former queen?

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a queen ant is the super ant of the colony; German über means super

explanation.surface: A spirited ex-monarch, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as EX-ÜBER-ANT: a former super-ant, the queen of a colony, not a royal.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant describes someone full of energy and high spirits.

clue.text: Reportedly drove squirrel away

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard said rather than written

parts.note: a drove is a crowd or horde, as of cattle or people

explanation.surface: Someone, by all accounts, chased a squirrel off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drove' looks like a past tense verb but is the noun for a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To squirrel away is to store up a secret stash, like a hamster stockpiling food.

clue.text: We watch them endlessly recount untruths

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to recount a story is to tell it
untruths are lies

explanation.surface: A complaint about people who keep spinning falsehoods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims TELL to TEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tellies is British slang for television sets, which viewers look at.

clue.text: Deny being close to manager O'Neill after reversal

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the word manager
after reversal means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Eugene O'Neill was the American playwright

explanation.surface: A football manager called O'Neill denies something after his team's setback.
explanation.walkthrough: Martin O'Neill was a football manager, but the needed O'Neill is playwright Eugene, turned round to ENEGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Renegue is a variant spelling of renege, to go back on a promise or deny a commitment.

clue.text: Conspicuous poverty traps

indicators.note: traps means the word poverty holds the answer within it

explanation.surface: Poverty catches people in obvious, visible ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, not hidden.

clue.text: Stop man at newspaper being fumigated

parts.note: split as S + top man at newspaper: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
the top man at a newspaper is its editor, ED

explanation.surface: A worker at a newspaper is told to halt while premises are being sprayed.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Stop' as S + 'top': S is read as its element, sulphur, and the top man at a newspaper is the editor, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning sulphur was a traditional fumigant, so to be sulphured is to be treated with its fumes.

clue.text: With which to shoot gnu?

parts.note: the word gnu is what you get if you scatter the letters of gun

explanation.surface: A hunter's question about the right weapon for an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: the answer read as an instruction, scatter GUN, produces the clue's word.
explanation.definitionFit: A scattergun is a shotgun, a firearm that sprays pellets widely.

clue.text: Careful doctor reeled a bit

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cautious physician wobbled slightly on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun but is the verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate means done with careful thought, unhurried and considered.

clue.text: Top man of high calibre?

parts.note: Top is the circus Big Top, and high calibre hints at a large gun firing a person

explanation.surface: Praise for an excellent leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The Big Top is a circus tent; calibre is the bore of a gun, so the star of the show is fired from a cannon.
explanation.definitionFit: This circus performer is shot from a cannon high across the Big Top.

clue.text: Guillotined European aristocrats

parts.note: guillotined means headless, and nob is slang for the head, so nob-less

explanation.surface: French Revolution nobles losing their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: NOB is slang for a head, so the beheaded are 'NOB-LESS'.
explanation.definitionFit: The noblesse is the nobility as a class, the aristocracy collectively.

clue.text: None left, you can be sure of that

definitions.meaning: if none is to the left, every one must be to the right

definitions.text: you can be sure of that
definitions.meaning: an assurance that everything is fine and certain

explanation.surface: A reassurance that nothing remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a reassurance that things are fine, and literally says every one is on the right.

clue.text: I bet voles, when excited, show signs of arousal

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cheeky bet about what amorous rodents leave behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Love bites are the marks left by passionate kissing or sucking of the skin.

clue.text: City which is very pleasant after end of June

indicators.note: after places the pleasant word following the end of June
end of means the final letter of June

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A city that turns delightful once summer is under way.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice is the Italian city built on canals in a lagoon.

clue.text: Sadly, Hibs wingers dismissed as "unprepared"

indicators.note: wingers are the outside letters, and dismissing them leaves the middles of both words

explanation.surface: A Hibernian football report: the wide players sent off for being poorly drilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Hibs is Hibernian, an Edinburgh football club; football wingers suggest players, but here they are the end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad-lib is said off the cuff, improvised without preparation.

clue.text: Group travel document with two pages missing

indicators.note: pages are abbreviated P, so two of them are removed

parts.note: a passport is the document needed for foreign travel

explanation.surface: A damaged passport for a group trip.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is the usual abbreviation for pages; both P's are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To assort is to sort into classes or groups, to classify.

clue.text: Answer needles terribly rude man in tights

indicators.note: needles means pierces, so the answer abbreviation is pushed into the other letters
terribly suggests the letters of rude are badly arranged

explanation.surface: Someone retorts to an annoyingly impolite man in hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffle gives DEUR, which the abbreviation splits after its first letter. 'man in tights' is a ballet dancer, not a superhero.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseur is a male ballet dancer, who typically performs in tights.

clue.text: May I, perhaps, go out?

definitions.meaning: the first of May is an example of a day on the calendar
to go out with someone is to court or see them

explanation.surface: A polite request for permission to leave the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The I is the Roman numeral one, making 'May I' the 1st of May.
explanation.definitionFit: May 1 is a calendar day; going out with someone means seeing them romantically.

clue.text: Perhaps top deck is better upholstered

parts.note: the upper deck of a double-decker bus
a deck is one tier, or level, of a vehicle

explanation.surface: A furniture comparison: the upper deck has plusher seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better upholstered' is a jokey way of saying curvier, with more bust.
explanation.definitionFit: Bustier is the comparative of busty, so someone better upholstered has a fuller figure.

clue.text: Northumbrian monk hiding drug in obvious place

indicators.note: hiding something in an obvious place means putting it under the bed, so in a down clue the drug sits below

parts.note: the bed is the obvious place to hide things, underneath it
E is short for ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: A monk caught stashing drugs where anyone would look.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, E sits under BED, the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable Bede was an Anglo-Saxon monk and historian at Jarrow in Northumbria.

clue.text: Beats Mo by seconds

parts.note: a mo is a moment, as is a tick

explanation.surface: An athlete called Mo wins a race by a few seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo suggests runner Mo Farah, but here it is informal British for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock's ticks are the beats that mark time passing.

clue.text: He's rotund rustic with jutting jaw

indicators.note: rustic means rough and unrefined, so the letters are rearranged crudely

explanation.surface: A description of a plump country bumpkin with a prominent chin.
explanation.definitionFit: An undershot jaw has the lower jaw projecting beyond the upper.
